newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine post office bombing leaves one injured.
newsitem.headline: Argentine post office bombing leaves one injured.

text.p: A bomb exploded at a privately owned Argentine post office on Thursday, seriously injuring one person, a company official said.

"We heard an explosion, according to the police it was apparently a parcel," Juan Marco Manes, an official at mail firm Cargo Correo Privado SA, told local television, "Only one person was injured, an older person about 40 years old."
Argentine television showed special police preparing to detonate what was feared to be a second explosive device at the post office in the Buenos Aires district of Constitucion.
The explosion came amid controversial plans by President Carlos Menem's government to privatise the state post office by decree.

The sale of the state post and telecommunications company ENCOTESA has been a political hot potato since former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's mid-1995 allegations of attempts to monopolise the Argentine postal service.
Central to Cavallo's accusations is businessman Alfredo Yabran, whom the former minister said built a private postal empire for criminal ends. Yabran denies the charges.
Asked to whom Cargo belonged, Manes said it did not belong to any particular economic group.
